p: בַּתַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת יֵרָא:
In Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of Parashat Vayeira:
"אָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַהוּ שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם כְּשֶׁהוּא מְהַלֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי?
What is the halakhah regarding a Jew accepting upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven while walking, etc.?
אָסוּר וְכוּלֵי, אֶלָּא יַעֲמוֹד בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וִיכַוֵּין לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם וְכוּלֵי,
It is forbidden, etc.; rather let him stand in one place and direct his heart to Heaven, etc.,
וּכְשֶׁמַּתְחִיל 'וְאָהַבְתָּ' – רָצָה מְהַלֵּךְ, רָצָה עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי".
and when he begins 'Ve-Ahavta' (and you shall love)—if he wishes he may walk, if he wishes he may stand, etc."
.] שַׁיָּיכוּת הֲלָכָה זוֹ לְרֹאשׁ הַפָּרָשָׁה
The connection of this halakhah to the opening of our Torah portion
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "לֶךְ לְךָ – לְגַרְמָךְ וְכוּלֵי, לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
is based on what is written in the holy Zohar: ''Go for yourself'—for your own sake, to rectify your own spiritual rung,' see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיְתָה אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Meaning that the attribute of Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, was the love of Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי";
as it is written: 'the seed of Avraham who loved Me' (Isaiah 41:8);
וְכָךְ הִיא הַמִּדָּה: לִהְיוֹת מְהַלֵּךְ מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא,
and such is the dynamic of this attribute: to continually progress and walk from rung to rung,
לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל פַּעַם יוֹתֵר בְּמִדָּתוֹ.
becoming progressively more clarified each time within one's divine trait.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְנָתַתִּי לְךָ מַהְלְכִים בֵּין הָעֹמְדִים וְגוֹמֵר",
And as written: 'and I will give you free access among these that stand by' (Zechariah 3:7),
דְּמַלְאָכִים הֵם עוֹמְדִים,
for the angels are stationary 'standers,'
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מְהַלֵּךְ תָּמִיד מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה.
whereas man must perpetually walk and ascend from level to level.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד לָצֵאת וְלָבוֹא",
And as we find with Moshe our Teacher who stated: 'I can no longer go out and come in' (Deuteronomy 31:2),
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
indicating that he had no further role in this world,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לָצֵאת, לֹא יוּכַל לָבוֹא לְדַרְגָּא גְּבוֹהָה יוֹתֵר.
since if he could no longer go forth, he could not advance into an even higher spiritual tier.

h: Spiritual perfection and the Midrashic interpretation

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לֶךְ לְךָ" – לְאַתְקָנָא גַּרְמָךְ, לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ;
And this is what is stated: ''Go for yourself'—to rectify yourself, to elevate your own spiritual rung;
וְזֶה שֶׁהֵבִיא, שֶׁבְּיִחוּד ה' בְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם,
and this explains what the Midrash brings: that at the unification of Hashem in accepting the yoke of Heaven,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
wherein one demonstrates and acknowledges that all is from Hashem, blessed be He,
צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת עוֹמֵד וּמְכַוֵּין לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם בְּאֵימָה וְיִרְאָה.
one must stand stationary and direct his heart to Heaven in awe and fear.
כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל "וְאָהַבְתָּ" – רָצָה מְהַלֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי,
Yet when one commences 'Ve-Ahavta'—if he wishes he may walk, etc.,
שֶׁבְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׁם הָעֵסֶק לִהְיוֹת מְהַלֵּךְ מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה לְבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
because within the love of Hashem the core task is to be a mover from rung to rung to refine oneself,
וּלְכָךְ רָצָה מְהַלֵּךְ רָצָה עוֹמֵד כְּפִי מַצַּב עֲבוֹדָתוֹ;
and therefore he may walk or stand according to the state of his divine service;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "לֶךְ לְךָ".
and this is the essence of 'Go for yourself.'

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 2:4: “Therefore he said, “I will give you those who walk among these who stand” (Zechariah 3:7). The angels are called those who stand, for they cannot walk: since they cannot go out, they cannot come in either. The souls of the righteous are called those who walk. This is what Rabbi Meir meant by Israel’s first advantage: they are guarded, while the angels are the guardians and do not need to be guarded. Needing to be guarded can itself be an advantage; the angels, by contrast, guard and are not guarded. The proof is not that, because they guard Israel, they are subordinate to them. After all, we also find, “The Lord is your guardian” (Psalms 121:5), and, in Vayetzei, “I will guard you wherever you go” (Genesis 28:15). Rather, he meant that the angels possess the power of guarding without having any fear that would require them to be guarded as well. Every created being that possesses an advantage also has a corresponding deficiency, which it fears and against which it needs protection. For the angels to have the power of guarding without any possibility of going out into harm is itself a deficiency. This reasoning does not apply to the blessed God.”

sourceExcerpt.en: Therefore he said, “I will give you those who walk among these who stand” (Zechariah 3:7). The angels are called those who stand, for they cannot walk: since they cannot go out, they cannot come in either. The souls of the righteous are called those who walk. This is what Rabbi Meir meant by Israel’s first advantage: they are guarded, while the angels are the guardians and do not need to be guarded. Needing to be guarded can itself be an advantage; the angels, by contrast, guard and are not guarded. The proof is not that, because they guard Israel, they are subordinate to them. After all, we also find, “The Lord is your guardian” (Psalms 121:5), and, in Vayetzei, “I will guard you wherever you go” (Genesis 28:15). Rather, he meant that the angels possess the power of guarding without having any fear that would require them to be guarded as well. Every created being that possesses an advantage also has a corresponding deficiency, which it fears and against which it needs protection. For the angels to have the power of guarding without any possibility of going out into harm is itself a deficiency. This reasoning does not apply to the blessed God.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 6: “The meaning is as my revered grandfather, of blessed memory, explained. The service of the angels on high cannot truly be credited to them as their own achievement, because they have no choice to act against His will and no obstacles they must overcome. They do not even desire what is outside His will, as it is said of them, “Wherever the spirit would go, they would go; they did not turn as they went” (Ezekiel 1:12). They have no inclination toward what is outside His will, so their service cannot be called the labor of their own hands. This is what the angels’ banners signify: their service follows a fixed order, in which they can neither lose nor gain. Israel is different: “I will give you those who walk among these who stand” (Zechariah 3:7). Israel is called one who walks, able to go from level to level without being confined to one fixed order, and able to gain through its service. It is true that it can also lose, God forbid, but it can also gain. This explains Israel’s desire for banners: everything they had acquired through their service should be established in an order that would prevent its loss. Yet they also wished to remain walkers, able to acquire more. Their principal wish to resemble the angels was that they should not lose what they had already acquired.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sefer HaZikhronot 8:6: “The matter of unifications is what they said: “When you pray, know before whom you pray.” This comes through recognizing that one is as though standing before the King. It is contemplation of His unity, which our Sages called “acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven,” as explained above. All these matters were known and were not hidden from Rabbi Yitzchak bar Sheshet. They are an obligation upon each person according to his condition: to deepen the intention of the heart in prayer so that it is an act of service before the blessed God, intending nothing for oneself but only for the honor of Heaven.”

If a congregation joins and forms one association with this intention of crowning the one God over themselves, that congregation will possess complete wholeness without division. Even if one states a halakhic teaching and another disagrees and rules the opposite, they are nevertheless joined at the root, where their words contain no division, since their intention is one. As the Talmud says: “Both those who said to kindle and those who said not to kindle intended the same thing”; and “These and those are the words of the living God.””

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: קַבָּלַת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם כְּשֶׁהוּא מְהַלֵּךְ הַיְינוּ: שֶׁרַק עַל הַגָּוֶון הוּא מַמְלִיךְ עָלָיו אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַד אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבוֹר וִיהַלֵּךְ אֶת הַמַּעֲבָר וְיַשִּׂיג חֵפֶץ לִבּוֹ, וְאָז יִתְפַּשֵּׁט לוֹ בָּהּ; וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ שֶׁאָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן. אָכֵן הַקַּבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם תִּהְיֶה מֵעוֹמֶק הַלֵּב בִּקְבִיעוּת – בָּזֶה יַחְפּוֹץ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְאִם יִתְחַבְּרוּ כְּנֵסִיָּה וְיַעֲשׂוּ אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת בְּזוֹ הַכַּוָּנָה לְהַמְלִיךְ עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת ה' אֶחָד, אֲזַי יִהְיֶה בְּזוֹ הַכְּנֵסִיָּה שְׁלֵימוּת גָּמוּר בְּלִי שׁוּם פֵּירוּד; וְאַף אִם יֹאמַר אֶחָד דְּבַר הֲלָכָה וַחֲבֵירוֹ יַחֲלוֹק עָלָיו וְיִפְסוֹק הַהֲלָכָה הֵיפֶךְ מִמֶּנּוּ, עִם כָּל זֶה מוּתְאָמִים הֵם בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ וְשָׁם אֵין בְּדִבְרֵיהֶם שׁוּם הִתְחַלְּקוּת, מֵאַחַר שֶׁכַּוָּנָתָם אֶחָד, וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּשַּׁ"ס (פְּסָחִים נג עַמּוּד ב): "בֵּין שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַדְלִיק וּבֵין שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַדְלִיק – שְׁנֵיהֶם לְדָבָר אֶחָד נִתְכַּוְּנוּ", וְ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים".
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Accepting the kingdom of Heaven while walking means crowning the blessed God over oneself only outwardly, until one passes through the passage and obtains the desire of one’s heart, after which one will give oneself free expansion in it. They said it is forbidden to act in this way. Rather, acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven must come from the depth of the heart as a fixed commitment; this is what the blessed God desires. If a congregation joins and forms one association with this intention of crowning the one God over themselves, that congregation will possess complete wholeness without division. Even if one states a halakhic teaching and another disagrees and rules the opposite, they are nevertheless joined at the root, where their words contain no division, since their intention is one. As the Talmud says: “Both those who said to kindle and those who said not to kindle intended the same thing”; and “These and those are the words of the living God.”

h: The Midrashic interpretation and the Gemara’s teaching

p: וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא:
And it states afterward in Midrash Tanchuma:
"'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ' – אֵין כְּתִיב 'וַאֲשִׂימְךָ' אֶלָּא 'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ',
''And I will make you'—it is not written 'and I will place you' but 'and I will make you';
אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹתְךָ אֲנִי בּוֹרֵא בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
He said to him: you do I create as a brand-new creation,
כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'וַיַּעַשׂ וְגוֹמֵר'".
in the manner of that which is stated: 'And He made, etc.'
.] וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד ב):
And this is based upon what they said in the Gemara (Nedarim 32b):
בַּתְּחִלָּה הִמְלִיכוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל רְמַ"ג אֵבָרִים
Initially the Holy One gave him dominion over 243 limbs,
וּלְבַסּוֹף עַל רְמַ"ח,
and ultimately over 248 limbs,
וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: שְׁתֵּי עֵינַיִם, שְׁתֵּי אָזְנַיִם, וּמִילָה;
and these extra five are: two eyes, two ears, and the organ of circumcision;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַף הָאֵבָרִים הָאֵלּוּ – עֵינָיו וְאָזְנָיו שֶׁאֵינָם בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ –
meaning that even these organs—his eyes and ears which naturally are not under voluntary control—
יִהְיוּ גַּם כֵּן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
shall likewise be under his sacred governance,
שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי אִם דְּבַר מִצְוָה (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַ"ן).
such that he shall neither hear nor see anything except a matter of mitzvah (as the Ran wrote).

h: Your eyes shall see your Teacher

p: וְהוּא עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת מוֹרֶיךָ",
And this reflects what is stated: 'and your eyes shall see your Teacher' (Isaiah 30:20),
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּרְאֶה יִלְמוֹד מִזֶּה אֵיזֶה דָבָר לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which means that whatever a person beholds, he learns from it some lesson for the service of Hashem,
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי לֹא לְחִנָּם הֶרְאוּ לוֹ דָּבָר זֶה,
for surely not in vain was this sight shown to him from Heaven,
רַק כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּלְמוֹד מִזֶּה דֶּרֶךְ ה';
rather so that he derive from it a path in the service of Hashem;
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׁמַע יִלְמוֹד מִזֶּה לְדַרְכֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה,
and likewise whatever he hears, he learns from it for paths of divine service,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאָזְנֶיךָ תִּשְׁמַעְנָה דָבָר מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ [לֵאמֹר] זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ",
in the manner stated: 'And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying: This is the way, walk in it' (Isaiah 30:21),
וְהוּא שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁלֹּא לְחִנָּם הִמְצִיא לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע זֶה הַדָּבָר,
which means he realizes that Hashem did not bring this sound to his ears without purpose,
וּבְוַדַּאי הוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּלְמוֹד מִזֶּה דֶּרֶךְ ה'.
and it is certainly so that he learn from it the way of Hashem.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אֵיזֶהוּ חָכָם? הַלּוֹמֵד מִכָּל אָדָם",
And this explains the teaching: 'Who is wise? He who learns from every person,' (Avot 4:1),
וְהַיְינוּ מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׁמַע וְיִרְאֶה יִלְמוֹד, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְכַוֵּין לְלַמְּדוֹ;
meaning that from everything he hears and sees he learns, even if the other person did not intend to teach him;
וְזֶה זָכָה אַחַר הַמִּילָה לִהְיוֹת נַעֲשָׂה בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
and this Avraham attained following circumcision, becoming a brand-new creation,
שֶׁעֵינָיו וְאָזְנָיו יִרְאוּ וְיִשְׁמְעוּ רַק דְּבַר מִצְוָה, לִלְמוֹד דֶּרֶךְ ה'.
such that his eyes and ears perceive and hear only matters of mitzvah to discern the path of Hashem.

Who is he that is honored? He who honors his fellow human beings as it is said: “For I honor those that honor Me, but those who spurn Me shall be dishonored” (I Samuel 2:30).”

He who rejoices in his lot, as it is said: “You shall enjoy the fruit of your labors, you shall be happy and you shall prosper” (Psalms 128:2) “You shall be happy” in this world, “and you shall prosper” in the world to come. Who is he that is honored? He who honors his fellow human beings as it is said: “For I honor those that honor Me, but those who spurn Me shall be dishonored” (I Samuel 2:30).”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Poked Akarim 6:8: “The community of Israel also has a hold in the Oral Torah. Even every unlearned person in Israel possesses some element of wisdom that belongs to the Oral Torah, although in him it is entirely concealed. Concerning the future it is said, “They shall all know [Me, from the least of them to the greatest]” (Jeremiah 31:33): the knowledge within them will emerge from concealment into revelation. Therefore the Zohar says that even an ordinary person’s words may be significant, and sometimes a pearl is found in a poor person’s basket. Throughout the Talmud we find, “This is what people say,” and their sayings are words of Torah; likewise the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6a) cites “a certain person who used to say,” and these are words of Torah. This is what they said, “Who is wise? One who learns from every person” (Avot 4:1): each person has some new element of wisdom that belongs particularly to the root of his soul and can be learned from him. “You are called adam, whereas the nations of the world are not called adam” (Yevamot 61a): here the point is that each member of Israel has a particular element of Oral Torah belonging to his soul’s root. A discerning person can learn it from him even if he himself knows nothing of it. But “those who seek the Lord understand everything” (Proverbs 28:5), and they can discern, through his conversations and words about worldly matters, some wisdom of his soul’s root that is concealed within them.”

sourceExcerpt.en: The community of Israel also has a hold in the Oral Torah. Even every unlearned person in Israel possesses some element of wisdom that belongs to the Oral Torah, although in him it is entirely concealed. Concerning the future it is said, “They shall all know [Me, from the least of them to the greatest]” (Jeremiah 31:33): the knowledge within them will emerge from concealment into revelation. Therefore the Zohar says that even an ordinary person’s words may be significant, and sometimes a pearl is found in a poor person’s basket. Throughout the Talmud we find, “This is what people say,” and their sayings are words of Torah; likewise the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6a) cites “a certain person who used to say,” and these are words of Torah. This is what they said, “Who is wise? One who learns from every person” (Avot 4:1): each person has some new element of wisdom that belongs particularly to the root of his soul and can be learned from him. “You are called adam, whereas the nations of the world are not called adam” (Yevamot 61a): here the point is that each member of Israel has a particular element of Oral Torah belonging to his soul’s root. A discerning person can learn it from him even if he himself knows nothing of it. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 3:10: “The meaning is this: when Abraham saw that they give way before one another, he understood that the blessed God had not concealed Himself completely. He had therefore established two opposites, so that through both of them people would recognize that there is One above them who rules them, and would direct their attention only to Him. For this reason the blessed God also established male and female throughout the world. Likewise it is written, “Lift your eyes on high and see: Who created these?” (Isaiah 40:26). “These” means all the particulars that the blessed God established in the world. “Who” is the place that stands open to questioning: a person should seek to know who created these. For this purpose the blessed God created all the particulars called “these.” As is taught in the introduction to the holy Zohar (1b), and as was explained in Bereishit, the blessed God desires that created beings ask who the Creator is. He therefore created opposing things in the world.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה: שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה שֶׁהֵם מִתְבַּטְּלִים זֶה מִפְּנֵי זֶה, הֵבִין מִזֶּה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא הִסְתִּיר עַצְמוֹ לְגַמְרֵי; לָזֶה הִצִּיב שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶם וּמוֹשֵׁל בָּהֶם וְלֹא יַבִּיטוּ רַק אֵלָיו. וּלְזֶה גַּם כֵּן הֶעֱמִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם בְּכָל דָּבָר זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה. וְכִדְכְתִיב גַּם כֵּן (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ מ, כו): "שְׂאוּ מָרוֹם עֵינֵיכֶם וּרְאוּ מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה": "אֵלֶּה" הַיְינוּ כָּל הַפְּרָטִים שֶׁהִצִּיב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם, וּ"מִי" הוּא אֲתַר דְּקַיְימָא לִשְׁאֵלָה, שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ הָאָדָם לָדַעַת: מִי בָּרָא אֵלֶּה. וּלְזֶה הַמְּכֻוָּון בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הַפְּרָטִים הַנִּקְרָאִים "אֵלֶּה", וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּהַקְדָּמַת זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (א עַמּוּד ב) (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית) שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ שֶׁיִּשְׁאֲלוּ הַבְּרוּאִים מִי הוּא הַבּוֹרֵא, וְלָכֵן בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דְּבָרִים הָפְכִיִּים בָּעוֹלָם.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: The meaning is this: when Abraham saw that they give way before one another, he understood that the blessed God had not concealed Himself completely. He had therefore established two opposites, so that through both of them people would recognize that there is One above them who rules them, and would direct their attention only to Him. For this reason the blessed God also established male and female throughout the world. Likewise it is written, “Lift your eyes on high and see: Who created these?” (Isaiah 40:26). “These” means all the particulars that the blessed God established in the world. “Who” is the place that stands open to questioning: a person should seek to know who created these. For this purpose the blessed God created all the particulars called “these.” As is taught in the introduction to the holy Zohar (1b), and as was explained in Bereishit, the blessed God desires that created beings ask who the Creator is. He therefore created opposing things in the world.

h: A convert who converts is like a newborn infant

p: וְאַף שֶׁבְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה נַעֲשָׂה אַחַר הַמִּילָה,
And although becoming a new creation occurred in practice after circumcision,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְבָמוֹת כב עַמּוּד א): "גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי",
as written (Yevamot 22a): 'A convert who converts is like a newborn infant,'
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" שֶׁבּוֹרֵא אוֹתוֹ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
nonetheless before Hashem, once He promised him 'and I will make you a great nation'—that He creates him anew—
כְּבָר זָכָה בָּזֶה תֵּיכֶף.
he already merited this immediately from that promise.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת) בְּשֵׁם תַּרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס (וּלְפָנֵינוּ לֵיתָא בְּאוּנְקְלוֹס):
And as the Ramban of blessed memory wrote (in Shemot) in the name of Targum Onkelos (though absent in our standard texts):
תַּרְגּוּם "אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה" – "אֶהֱא עִם מַאן דְּאֶהֱא", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
the translation of 'Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh' is: 'I will be with whomever I will be,' see there;
וְהַיְינוּ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַבְטִיחַ שֶׁאֶהְיֶה עִמּוֹ לֶעָתִיד,
meaning that once Hashem promises that He will be with him in the future,
כְּבָר מֵעֵת הַהַבְטָחָה אֲנִי עִמּוֹ,
already from the moment of the promise He is with him;
וְעַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן" לֶעָתִיד;
reflecting what is stated: 'and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious' in the future;
וְשֵׁם אֶהְיֶ"ה, אַף שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל הֶעָתִיד, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹפִיעַ תֵּיכֶף בַּהֹוֶה.
and the Name Ehyeh, although pointing to the future, shines immediately in the present.
וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" –
And so Hashem said to him: 'And I will make you a great nation'—
"וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ", שֶׁאֲנִי בּוֹרֵא אוֹתְךָ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים בִּרְשׁוּתְךָ גַּם כֵּן;
'and I will make you,' meaning I create you as a new being such that these five organs are likewise in your governance;
וְזֶהוּ "לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל", שֶׁהוּא שֶׁנִּכְלַל בּוֹ אֻמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּמִדַּת "גָּדוֹל",
and this is 'a great nation,' in that the nation of Israel is encompassed within him, bound at the root in the attribute 'Gadol',
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
which indicates boundless infinity up to the Root.
וּכְבָר זָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מֵהַבְטָחָה זוֹ לִהְיוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה וְגָדוֹל.
And already from this promise Avraham merited to become the chariot to the attribute of Gedulah and Gadol.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Shemot 7:1: “Their question “What is His name?” means that they knew their deeds did not yet make them fit for redemption, and that it was also before the time, as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah. They would therefore ask: through which of His qualities will He redeem them? The blessed God answered Moses with the name “Ehyeh asher Ehyeh.” Ehyeh signifies “I am destined,” and so forth. The blessed God said: “I will be with the one with whom I will be”—with the one with whom I will be in the future, it is already felt in the present. This resembles “I will be gracious to the one to whom I will be gracious,” as explained in Lech Lecha, ois six. He therefore told him to speak to them the name Ehyeh, indicating the future revelation of Atika that they would merit at the splitting of the sea, as the holy Zohar says concerning the maidservant who saw at the sea. Likewise at the giving of Torah, “Face to face”: Israel saw there what Ezekiel did not see. Through his telling them the name Ehyeh, they would immediately feel a foretaste of that holiness.”

sourceExcerpt.en: Their question “What is His name?” means that they knew their deeds did not yet make them fit for redemption, and that it was also before the time, as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah. They would therefore ask: through which of His qualities will He redeem them? The blessed God answered Moses with the name “Ehyeh asher Ehyeh.” Ehyeh signifies “I am destined,” and so forth. The blessed God said: “I will be with the one with whom I will be”—with the one with whom I will be in the future, it is already felt in the present. This resembles “I will be gracious to the one to whom I will be gracious,” as explained in Lech Lecha, ois six. He therefore told him to speak to them the name Ehyeh, indicating the future revelation of Atika that they would merit at the splitting of the sea, as the holy Zohar says concerning the maidservant who saw at the sea. Likewise at the giving of Torah, “Face to face”: Israel saw there what Ezekiel did not see. Through his telling them the name Ehyeh, they would immediately feel a foretaste of that holiness.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 69:1: ““Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him.” Scripture praises Isaac’s sowing so greatly to indicate that, at the very beginning, at the time of sowing, he recognized all the growth that would later emerge from it. He saw clearly that no hardship borne by Israel fails to produce a great salvation, as it is written: “I thank You, Lord, that You were angry with me; Your anger will turn away and You will comfort me.” In truth, within the hardship itself lies the beginning of salvation’s illumination. This is the meaning of David digging the channels to raise the deep, as the Talmud says: when he saw that it had descended too far, he said, “The higher it stands, the more it waters the world.” He dug to awaken from the depth of the clarification that will be revealed in the future: that Israel never suffered, for the flow of His light never ceased at any time. All the illuminations of salvation that now shine in this world are drawn from that raising of the deep. The salvations that sometimes occur now are only an illumination of the comprehensive salvation that will be in the future. Therefore Isaac’s blessing enumerates all the salvations—supporting the fallen, healing the sick, and so forth—and concludes with resurrection. All those good things grow even now from the great illumination of the future salvation called resurrection, when the blessed God will show explicitly that Israel never suffered at all. From this a salvation is sometimes awakened in this world too. Isaac therefore reckoned all the salvations from the time of sowing, for he already saw the future salvation then, until the sowing itself was counted as salvation in his eyes.”

h: The Midrashic interpretation and Avraham’s devotion

p: וּמִטַּעַם זֶה פָּתַח בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בַּפָּסוּק:
And for this reason Midrash Rabbah opened this parashah with the verse:
"שִׁמְעִי בַת וּרְאִי וְהַטִּי אָזְנֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear, etc.,” (Psalms 45:11),
שֶׁהוּא נִדְרָשׁ עַל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא;
which is expounded concerning Avraham our Father, and as also brought in Midrash Tanchuma;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לוֹ שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּבָרֵר עַצְמוֹ בְּמִדָּתוֹ וּבְכָל הַמִּדּוֹת,
meaning that Hashem commanded him that from his own initiative he must refine himself in his attribute and in all attributes,
שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע וְיִרְאֶה רַק עֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
so that he hear and see solely the service of Hashem,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר לוֹ: "לֶךְ לְךָ" – לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ;
and concerning this it was said to him: 'Go for yourself'—to elevate your own spiritual rung;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחוֹ בֶּעָתִיד: "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ", שֶׁאֲנִי בּוֹרֵא אוֹתְךָ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים גַּם כֵּן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
and Hashem promised him regarding the future: 'and I will make you'—that I create you a new being such that these five organs are likewise in his control,
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁיְּבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ.
namely after he refines himself according to his own strength.

The beneficial counsel for a person even here is to diminish and restrain this domain according to his capacity. He can then say, “Go to the Craftsman who made me,” who did not give me greater power. When a person restrains himself according to his capacity, through great labor in service, as far as his reach extends, then in the domain where human power does not reach or rule—as in procreation, which necessarily involves forgetfulness and concealment—he can rely on the plea “Go to the Craftsman who made me.” That is, the blessed God will complete the matter for his good. Consequently this person will see that nothing in the world exists apart from God: every thing has a connection to the blessed God, who created everything, governs everything, and rules everything. The person, on his own side, has no independent power at all.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: The meaning is this: in this domain there is an extremely great expansion, forgetfulness, and concealment, to the extent that even a righteous person sometimes fathers a wicked person. The beneficial counsel for a person even here is to diminish and restrain this domain according to his capacity. He can then say, “Go to the Craftsman who made me,” who did not give me greater power. When a person restrains himself according to his capacity, through great labor in service, as far as his reach extends, then in the domain where human power does not reach or rule—as in procreation, which necessarily involves forgetfulness and concealment—he can rely on the plea “Go to the Craftsman who made me.” That is, the blessed God will complete the matter for his good. Consequently this person will see that nothing in the world exists apart from God: every thing has a connection to the blessed God, who created everything, governs everything, and rules everything. The person, on his own side, has no independent power at all.

h: The Divine covenant and wine and spiritual joy

p: וְשַׁיָּיכוּת זֶה לַמִּילָה הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר:
And the connection of this to circumcision is based on that which is stated:
"וְלֹא נָתַן ה' לָכֶם לֵב לָדַעַת וְעֵינַיִם לִרְאוֹת וְאָזְנַיִם לִשְׁמֹעַ וְגוֹמֵר,
“Yet Hashem has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, etc.,
וָאוֹלֵךְ אֶתְכֶם וְגוֹמֵר, לֶחֶם לֹא אֲכַלְתֶּם וְיַיִן וְשֵׁכָר לֹא שְׁתִיתֶם וְגוֹמֵר",
and I have led you, etc., bread you have not eaten, neither have you drunk wine or strong drink, etc.,” (Deuteronomy 29:3–5),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶם לֵב לָדַעַת, אָז זָכוּ לִהְיוֹת לָהֶם עֵינַיִם לִרְאוֹת,
meaning that once He granted them a heart to know, they then merited having eyes to see,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּרְאוּ רַק אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִלְמְדוּ מִכָּל הַבְּרִיּוֹת לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
namely that they see only Hashem and learn from all creations for His holy service,
עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין ק עַמּוּד ב): "'מַלְּפֵנוּ מִבַּהֲמוֹת אָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר' – אִלְמָלֵא לֹא נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה הָיִינוּ לְמֵדִין צְנִיעוּת וְכוּלֵי",

h: The forefathers and the written and oral Torah

p: וְזֶה שֶׁהִזְכִּיר שָׁם הַכָּתוּב הֲלִיכַת הַמִּדְבָּר, וְהַמָּן וְהַבְּאֵר:
And this explains why Scripture mentioned there the journey in the wilderness, the Manna, and the Well:
שֶׁזָּכוּ לַמָּן בִּזְכוּת מֹשֶׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ט עַמּוּד א),
for they merited the Manna in the merit of Moshe (Ta'anit 9a),
וְהַמָּן – "לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם",
and the Manna is 'bread from heaven,'
"לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי" – נַהֲמָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבִכְתָב,
'come, eat of my bread'—the bread of the Written Torah,
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
and Moshe our Teacher is the root of the Written Torah,
וּבוֹ טָעֲמוּ כָּל הַמַּאֲכָלִים, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הָאֲכִילוֹת;
and within it they tasted all foods, it being the spiritual root of all nourishment;
וְהַבְּאֵר, דְּאִיתָא (בַּמְּכִילְתָּא יִתְרוֹ): שֶׁהַבְּאֵר טוֹעֲמִין בּוֹ טַעַם יַיִן יָשָׁן וְכוּלֵי, טַעַם כָּל הַמַּמְתַּקִּים וְכוּלֵי,
and the Well, as taught (in the Mekhilta, Yitro): that in the Well they tasted the flavor of aged wine, etc., the taste of all sweet delicacies, etc.,
וְהוּא יַיִן מָסָכְתִּי – יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה,
and that is 'the wine I have mingled'—the wine of the Oral Torah,
וְזֶהוּ בִּזְכוּת מִרְיָם;

h: Since after forty years they merited a heart to know,

p: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁזָּכוּ אַחַר אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה לֵב לָדַעַת,
And since after forty years they merited a heart to know,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה עַמּוּד ב) מִפָּסוּק זֶה:
and as they derived (Avodah Zarah 5b) from this verse:
שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, לָא קָאֵים אִינִישׁ אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבֵּיהּ עַד אַרְבָּעִין שְׁנִין,
infer from this: a person does not fully grasp the mind of his master until forty years have elapsed,
מִמֵּילָא זָכוּ אָז שֶׁנִּיתַּן לָהֶם עֵינַיִם לִרְאוֹת וְאָזְנַיִם לִשְׁמֹעַ כָּאָמוּר.
consequently they merited then that there were given to them eyes to see and ears to hear as explained.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And likewise with Avraham our Father, peace be upon him,
דִּכְתִיב: "וּמָצָאתָ אֶת לְבָבוֹ נֶאֱמָן לְפָנֶיךָ וְכָרוֹת עִמּוֹ הַבְּרִית וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written: “And You found his heart faithful before You, and made a covenant with him, etc.,” (Nehemiah 9:8),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז זָכָה לְלֵב לָדַעַת,
meaning that then he merited a heart to know;
אָז זָכָה שֶׁהִמְלִיכוֹ עַל חֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ גַּם כֵּן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
then he merited that Hashem gave him dominion over the five organs to be under his voluntary rule,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְשַׂמְתָּ שְׁמוֹ אַבְרָהָם",
and as is stated: 'and made his name Avraham' (adding the letter Hei = 5),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז זָכָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי אִם דְּבַר מִצְוָה שֶׁיִּלְמוֹד לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
meaning that then he attained that they be in his control, neither hearing nor seeing anything but a mitzvah from which he derives divine service, as we stated.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5b: ‘Yet even Moses our teacher, who said this to the Jewish people, did not allude to the Jewish people until after forty years that they should have stated this request, as it is stated: “And I have led you forty years in the wilderness” (Deuteronomy 29:4), which shows that Moses was speaking forty years after the revelation at Sinai. And at that point it is written: “But the Lord has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, until this day” (Deuteronomy 29:3). Rabba said: Conclude from here that a person does not understand the opinion of his teacher until after forty years, as Moses said this to the Jewish people only after forty years of learning Torah.’

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sefer HaZikhronot 17:2: “The Raaya Meheimna says: “‘You shall know that I am the Lord your God’—this is the first commandment of all the commandments: to know the Holy One, blessed be He, in a general way, that there is a supreme ruler, the Master of the world, who created all the worlds. At the end of forty years of labor, He then taught them in a particular way. This is ‘Know today’: specifically today, when previously they had no permission. ‘That the Lord is God’—this is in a particular way, and many mysteries and secrets are contained in it. This and the first are all one matter: one in general and one in particular.” These are its words. This makes clear what I wrote: the commandment “Know” concerns particular knowledge, by way of the mystery and the secrets of Torah. The precision we noted in “today”—that it is not a command universally applicable like the generality of commandments—is likewise explicit here. They interpret it literally: “today,” after forty years of labor in Torah and commandments. These are the words of the Rambam that one should not enter the orchard until one has filled one’s belly with meat and wine from the revealed aspects of Torah and the commandments.”

sourceExcerpt.en: The Raaya Meheimna says: “‘You shall know that I am the Lord your God’—this is the first commandment of all the commandments: to know the Holy One, blessed be He, in a general way, that there is a supreme ruler, the Master of the world, who created all the worlds. At the end of forty years of labor, He then taught them in a particular way. This is ‘Know today’: specifically today, when previously they had no permission. ‘That the Lord is God’—this is in a particular way, and many mysteries and secrets are contained in it. This and the first are all one matter: one in general and one in particular.” These are its words. This makes clear what I wrote: the commandment “Know” concerns particular knowledge, by way of the mystery and the secrets of Torah. The precision we noted in “today”—that it is not a command universally applicable like the generality of commandments—is likewise explicit here. They interpret it literally: “today,” after forty years of labor in Torah and commandments. These are the words of the Rambam that one should not enter the orchard until one has filled one’s belly with meat and wine from the revealed aspects of Torah and the commandments.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ki Tavo 6: “This is “The Lord did not give you a heart to know”: after they had passed through many concealments in the wilderness, as it is written, “Who led you through the great and fearsome wilderness, with fiery serpents and scorpions,” indicating the concealments they experienced, they did not wish to remain in concealment. They broke through all the concealments and thereby clarified themselves as desiring only the will of the blessed God. God then says, “At forty, understanding.” They are called the generation of knowledge, and no generation is as beloved as the wilderness generation. The blessed God testified that even within concealment they were bound to Him and did not depart from His will by even a hair’s breadth. This is “The Lord did not give you a heart to know ... until this day.” Likewise, this portion says, “You have affirmed the Lord today to be your God,” and “The Lord has affirmed you today to be His treasured people.” My revered grandfather explained that he’emarta is related to the hem of a garment. As long as a garment has no hem, it is unfinished, and one can still add to or remove from it; when the hem is completed, the garment reaches its completion. Thus, after Israel clarified itself over forty years so that its entire purpose was “to be your God”—the honor of Heaven—God showed that His entire purpose was for Israel, and all Creation was for Israel, as the Tikkunei Zohar and the Midrash say: Israel arose in thought first.”

h: Avraham’s devotion and the Divine covenant

p: וּמִטַּעַם זֶה מְיוּשָּׁב גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָקְרוּ: לָמָּה לֹא מָל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה,
And for this reason that which scholars probed is resolved: why did Avraham not circumcise himself prior to being commanded,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה?
just as he fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given?
אַךְ הַמִּילָה הוֹעִילָה רַק אַחַר שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה עָלֶיהָ וְנֶאֱמַר לוֹ: "הְיֵה תָמִים" וְנַעֲשָׂה בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
However, circumcision was effective only after he was explicitly commanded concerning it and told 'be wholehearted' and became a new creation,
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁבֵּירֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ,
meaning after he had refined himself from his own initiative according to his capacity,
שֶׁזָּכָה אָז שֶׁהִמְלִיכוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים;
whereupon he merited that Hashem granted him dominion over the five organs;
אֲבָל קוֹדֶם לָזֶה לֹא הָיָה מִילָתוֹ כְּלוּם,
whereas prior to this, his circumcision would have achieved nothing,
וּכְמוֹ מוּלֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת דְּנִקְרָאוּ עֲרֵלִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לא עַמּוּד ב).
just like circumcised heathens who are still titled uncircumcised, as written in the Gemara (Nedarim 31b).
אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחוֹ כָּעֵת "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ", שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
However Hashem promised him at this juncture 'and I will make you'—that He will transform him into a new creation,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְהַרְגִּישׁ מֵעֵין זֶה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
so that he merit to feel a semblance of this transformative state as we explained.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Genesis, Lech Lecha 3: “"And God said unto Abraham: And as for you, you shall keep My covenant, you, and your seed after you throughout their generations." The inner reason Abraham did not perform the mitzvah of circumcision before being explicitly commanded, even though we find in the Gemara (Yoma 28b) that our father Abraham fulfilled even the rabbinic ordinance of Eiruv Tavshilin, is because all commandments serve as safeguards for man to walk in alignment with how God originally made man upright, and not tilt to an extreme but follow the balanced middle way; for if he becomes excessively immersed in one pursuit he will distort the straight path and stray from it; therefore our father Abraham kept all commandments prior to being formally commanded regarding them; however, the mitzvah of circumcision represents man actively rectifying the creation of Hashem, blessed be He, which was deliberately created with a deficiency; consequently, before being explicitly commanded he could not on his own initiative alter and rectify Hashem's creation, for it would have appeared, Heaven forbid, as though declaring: 'how ugly is this vessel which You have fashioned!'; therefore Hashem, blessed be He, showed him the birth of Ishmael, for even through his birth Abraham had fulfilled the will of Hashem, blessed be He, since with our father Abraham nothing was ever treated as merely optional or profane, rather he performed all his actions strictly in accordance with the divine will; and afterward he observed that the deeds of Ishmael were corrupt, and from this he understood that Hashem, blessed be He, deliberately established deficiency so that man should rectify it and have it credited to man's name; and through this he comprehended that there was indeed a designated place for the mitzvah of circumcision, and this he did not perceive until Ishmael grew up to be thirteen years of age; and immediately when he understood that there was room for the mitzvah of circumcision, Hashem, blessed be He, illuminated his mind and immediately gave him the commandment through an explicit utterance, demonstrating that such is His will: that the deeds of man should be revealed, and 'the labor of his hands he shall eat.'”

sourceExcerpt.en: "And God said unto Abraham: And as for you, you shall keep My covenant, you, and your seed after you throughout their generations." The inner reason Abraham did not perform the mitzvah of circumcision before being explicitly commanded, even though we find in the Gemara (Yoma 28b) that our father Abraham fulfilled even the rabbinic ordinance of Eiruv Tavshilin, is because all commandments serve as safeguards for man to walk in alignment with how God originally made man upright, and not tilt to an extreme but follow the balanced middle way; for if he becomes excessively immersed in one pursuit he will distort the straight path and stray from it; therefore our father Abraham kept all commandments prior to being formally commanded regarding them; sourceExcerpt.en: In truth, the Exodus clarifies this matter: the holiness of each Israelite soul individually, rather than only the general holiness derived from the patriarchs. “Let his men be numbered”: in the count of six hundred thousand, each is considered and counted on his own. I heard that this is the meaning of the census of Israel and the numbering of its people: each is a counted thing, important in himself, and is not nullified within the collective, for he has a particular power not found in everyone. They merited this individual holiness at the giving of Torah and through the Egyptian exile that preceded it. Concerning “a nation from within a nation,” our Sages said: like a fetus within its mother. Ezekiel explicitly calls the redemption from Egypt a birth: “As for your birth, on the day you were born,” and so forth. The Ari likewise explains in Pri Etz Chaim that Egypt was the mystery of gestation; examine it there at length.
